THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the Corporation aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.511/2013 dated 13.06.2014.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.26,46,223.25 an account of the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the claimant is that, on 30.01.2013 about 12.30 noon, while deceased was proceeding in front of NC: 2023:KHC:37504 KSRTC bus stand, Hunsur, the driver of KSRTC bus came in a high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased in front of entrance gate of bus stand.
As a result deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Government Hospital, thereafter refered to Vikram Jeev and thereafter to Vathsalya (Seetharanga)
Hospital, Mysore.
Deceased took treatment as inpatient and has undergone operations for the injuries sustained.
However, deceased could not recover and succumbed to the injuries on 15.02.2013.

In support of their case the wife of the deceased was examined as PW1 and EX.P1 to P123 were marked along with the complaint, FIR, spot mahazar, rough sketch, Motor vehicle accident report, mahazar of dead body, charge-sheet, death certificate, medical bills, 26 prescription, case sheet, six x-rays.
13 scan photos, postmortem report and the salary certificate.
The Court below had observed that after registering the claim petition the notice has been issued to the respondents.
In pursuance of the notice the respondents did not enter appearance and submitted objection statement in spite of service of notice and later they have been set ex-parte.
The Court below considering the evidence on record had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.10,60,000/-.
Aggrieved thereby, the Corporation is in appeal before this Court.

Learned counsel for the corporation submits that even if the respondents have not appeared before the Court, while granting the compensation, the Court has to consider the negligence and the involvement of the The Managing Director vs S. Rohini on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192141209/
2 vehicle just because the respondents were not appearing.
The Court below without any basis can not grant the compensation.

He submits that the Court below without recording any of the findings,
basing on the police records had granted compensation.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that even after service of the notice the respondents have conveniently kept quite.
The Tribunal basing on the evidence let in by the claimants had granted the compensation.
He submits that they have failed to appear before the Court below.

When they failed to appear before the Court they have no right to come before the Court and submit that the compensation that was awarded was not right and there was no proper appreciation of the evidence.
This Court having heard learned counsel on either side perused the entire material on record.
The date of the accident was on 30.01.2013 and the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 15.02.2013 nearly after 17 days he died.
He was in the hospital for all those 17 days but for reasons known to the claimant he had not marked any medical records before the Court below.

Though the respondent-Corporation had not appeared before the court below, when the Court below was passing the order on the merits it in an application filed under 166 of M.V. Act, the Court below ought to have considered the evidence and if on such evidence produced by the claimant.
If the Court is satisfied that there is negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus, then the Court ought to have passed the award.
But in this case the Court below had only relied on the police records and no medical records were filed before the Court below.
In that view of the matter balancing interest of both the parties, this Court deems it appropriate to remand the matter back to the MACT for fresh consideration.

6. Accordingly, the award dated 30.06.2014 in MVC No.511/2013 is set aside and the matter is remanded back to NC: 2023:KHC:37504 the MACT and it is left open to both the parties to lead evidence and file objections and without any further notice.
i) Appeal of the respondent-Corporation in MFA No.511/2017 is allowed by setting aside the award dated 30.06.2014 and the matter is remanded back to the Court below.
iii) Without any further notice both the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 08.11.2023.
The MACT shall dispose of the case within a period of six months from 08.11.2023.
iv) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the MACT forthwith and the same shall be kept in fixed deposit.
v) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
vi) No costs.
